name: New-Matter Setup Bot

parameters.content:
## New-Matter Setup Bot

### How it works

1. Polls Clio hourly for matters opened since the last check (tracked in n8n's own workflow memory, no external database) and safely skips every already-existing matter on first activation instead of processing your whole matter list at once.
2. For each new matter, finds or creates its Google Drive folder — reusing the same folder the Document-to-Matter Auto-Filer (PAC-58) falls back to creating on first document arrival — then builds out the firm's standard subfolder structure inside it.
3. Copies the internal document templates configured for that matter's practice area into the new folder and fills in basic merge fields (client name, matter number, open date).
4. Creates the firm's standard task checklist for that practice area in Clio, with due dates offset from the matter's open date.
5. Calculates and calendars intake deadlines in Clio from firm-entered rules for that practice area — never suggests or interprets a deadline itself.
6. Logs the whole setup to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet and emails staff a summary with links.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Set CLIO_BASE_URL and connect the Clio OAuth2 credential (reuse if already deployed for PAC-18/20/55/57/58).
- [ ] Set GENERATED_DOCS_FOLDER_ID to the same Drive folder PAC-57/58 use — matter folders live alongside generated documents.
- [ ] Edit DOC_TEMPLATE_MAP, TASK_LIST_MAP, and DEADLINE_RULE_MAP in the 'Determine Practice Area Setup Config' node to match your firm's own templates, task checklist, and deadline rules per practice area.
- [ ] Create the internal Google Doc templates referenced by TEMPLATE_*_DOC_ID variables (e.g. Matter Opening Checklist, Case Plan) and set those variables.
- [ ] Set GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID to the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (OPS1 / NTC-33) workflow ID.
- [ ] Set FIRM_STAFF_EMAIL and FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, and connect the SMTP credential.

### Customization

Adjust DEFAULT_FOLDERS in 'Build Standard Subfolder List' for your firm's folder structure, and the polling interval on the trigger node.

## Trigger and dedupe

Polls Clio hourly for open matters and filters to ones this workflow hasn't set up yet, using n8n's built-in workflow memory — no external database. First activation seeds every existing matter as already-seen instead of processing the whole matter list at once.

## Matter folder and subfolder tree

Finds or creates the matter's Drive folder (reusing PAC-58's folder if a document already arrived for this matter), then builds the firm's standard subfolder structure inside it.

## Practice-area setup lookup

Looks up which document templates, tasks, and deadline rules apply to this matter's practice area. Any of the three can be left unconfigured — the corresponding step is skipped, not blocked.

## Document template copy

Copies each configured internal template into the matter folder and fills in basic merge fields. Skipped if no templates are configured for this practice area.

## Task list assignment

Creates the firm's standard task checklist for this practice area in Clio, with due dates calculated from the matter's open date. Skipped if no task list is configured.

## Intake deadline calendaring

Calculates and creates calendar entries in Clio for firm-entered intake deadlines — same business-day math as the Court Deadline Calculator (NTC-16). Skipped if no deadline rules are configured. The firm owns every rule; nothing here is legal judgment.

## Summary, audit log, and staff notification

Builds one summary of everything set up for the matter, logs it to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet, and emails staff with links to the new folder and documents.

nodes.name: Poll For New Matters
nodes.notes:
Checks Clio for newly opened matters once an hour (n8n server timezone). Staff keep opening matters in Clio exactly as they do today — nothing changes for them; this just picks new ones up on the next poll.

Tighten to every 15 minutes ('*/15 * * * *') if matters need same-hour setup, or loosen to every few hours for a firm that opens matters in batches.

This is the only thing that starts a run — nothing else in this workflow fires on its own.

nodes.name: Fetch Open Matters From Clio
nodes.notes:
Fetches every currently-open matter — filtering to genuinely NEW ones happens next via n8n's own workflow memory, not a Clio date filter, since Clio's created-since query behavior wasn't confirmed live during authoring. Same 'fetch everything, dedupe locally' approach as the Duplicate-Contact Watchdog (PAC-55).

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58 — reuse it if already deployed.

The nested fields syntax (client{id,name}, practice_area{id,name}) follows Clio's documented sub-resource selection — verify the response shape against your own Clio account (Settings → API) and adjust the 'Split New Matters Into Items' node if a relation comes back differently.

Clio paginates results (default page size varies by plan); only the first page is fetched here. Fine for the solo/small-firm open-matter counts this template targets — a firm with several hundred simultaneously open matters would need to add pagination.

nodes.name: Filter To Newly Opened Matters
nodes.notes:
Marks a matter as seen the moment it's identified as new, before any setup work runs -- so if a later step in this run fails, that matter won't be silently retried forever on every future poll (it also won't be retried at all; check execution history if a run errors partway through and finish that matter's setup by hand).

bootstrap is true only on the very first run after activation, when every open matter gets seeded as already-seen instead of queued for setup.

nodes.name: If Has New Matters
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one matter this workflow hasn't set up yet) → process each one.
No (nothing new since the last poll, or this was the bootstrap run) → route to Skip.

nodes.name: Skip No New Matters
nodes.notes: Nothing new to set up this poll — expected for most hourly checks. No folders, documents, tasks, or calendar entries are created.

nodes.name: Split New Matters Into Items
nodes.notes: Reads client_name and practice_area off the nested relation objects Clio returns for client{id,name} / practice_area{id,name} -- confirm this matches your account's actual response shape (see notes on 'Fetch Open Matters From Clio') and adjust the field paths here if not.

nodes.name: Search For Existing Matter Folder
nodes.notes:
Checks whether this matter already has a Drive folder, under GENERATED_DOCS_FOLDER_ID -- the same folder the Document-to-Matter Auto-Filer (PAC-58) uses, so a matter never ends up with two different folders depending on which template got to it first.

Same Advanced Search / exact 'name =' query pattern as PAC-58's 'Search For Matter Folder' node, confirmed against n8n's own Google Drive node source there.

'Always Output Data' is on (Settings tab) -- a zero-match search (the normal case for a brand-new matter) would otherwise silently halt the whole run instead of proceeding to create the folder.

Credential: same 'Google Drive account' credential as PAC-57/58 — reuse it if already deployed.

nodes.name: Check Matter Folder Existence
nodes.notes: Determines whether the matter already has a Drive folder. If PAC-58 filed a document for this matter before this bot got to it, it won't need to create one — the next step reuses it.

nodes.name: If Matter Folder Found
nodes.notes:
Yes (PAC-58 or an earlier run already created this matter's folder) → go straight to building the subfolder tree in it.
No → create the matter's root folder first. Both branches converge on 'Build Standard Subfolder List'.

nodes.name: Create Matter Root Folder
nodes.notes:
Creates this matter's root Drive folder — same naming convention as PAC-58's 'Create New Matter Folder' node (display number + description), under the same GENERATED_DOCS_FOLDER_ID parent, so both templates always agree on where a matter's documents live.

Uses the same 'Google Drive account' credential as the search step. Parent folder is set via the top-level 'Parent Drive'/'Parent Folder' fields, not nested under Options — the lesson learned the hard way on PAC-57/58.

nodes.name: Build Standard Subfolder List
nodes.notes: Fans out into one item per standard subfolder -- 5 folders means 5 items reaching 'Create Matter Subfolder' below. Add or remove entries in DEFAULT_FOLDERS directly in this node's code.

nodes.name: Create Matter Subfolder
nodes.notes: Creates each standard subfolder inside the matter's root folder — runs once per item from 'Build Standard Subfolder List'. If this workflow ever reruns for the same matter (it shouldn't, due to the dedupe step), re-running this node would create duplicate subfolders — not destructive, just untidy; clean up manually if that ever happens.

nodes.name: Aggregate Folder Tree Setup
nodes.notes: Collapses the per-subfolder items back into one summary item for this matter, carrying the matter's own fields forward (they were dropped from $json once the Drive API responses replaced it).

nodes.name: Determine Practice Area Setup Config
nodes.notes: This is the one node to edit when onboarding a new firm — everything else in the workflow just executes whatever comes out of these three maps. A practice area missing from a map (or a doc template Variable left unset) safely skips that one step rather than erroring.

nodes.name: If Has Document Templates
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one document template configured for this practice area) → copy them in.
No → route to Skip. Both branches converge on 'Aggregate Document Setup Results'.

nodes.name: Skip No Document Templates
nodes.notes: No document templates configured for this matter's practice area — nothing copied. Add rows to DOC_TEMPLATE_MAP in 'Determine Practice Area Setup Config' if this practice area should have templates.

parameters.jsCode:
const { docs, doc_count, has_docs, tasks, task_count, has_tasks, deadline_rules, deadline_count, has_deadlines, ...meta } = $input.first().json;
return docs.map(d => ({ json: { ...meta, ...d } }));

nodes.name: Split Doc Template List Into Items
nodes.notes: Fans out into one item per configured document template.

nodes.name: Copy Doc Template To Matter Folder
nodes.notes:
Duplicates the internal template into the matter's root folder — same copy pattern as PAC-57's 'Copy Google Docs Template'. These are internal matter-setup documents (checklist, case plan), not client-facing paperwork — PAC-57 already handles client-facing intake documents.

Credential: same 'Google Drive account' credential as the folder steps above.

nodes.name: Build Doc Merge Requests
nodes.notes: Your internal template docs must contain these exact tags: {{matter_display_number}}, {{matter_description}}, {{client_name}}, {{practice_area}}, {{open_date}}. Set to 'Run Once for Each Item' so every configured document gets its own merge request, not just the first.

nodes.name: Update Doc Merge Fields
nodes.notes: Replaces every merge tag in the copied document — same direct Docs API call as PAC-57's 'Update Google Docs Merge Fields', since n8n's native Google Docs node has no find-and-replace operation. Reuses the 'Google Drive account' credential (Google Docs API must be enabled alongside Drive API in the same Cloud Console project). Uses 'Predefined Credential Type', not 'Generic' — Generic sends no Authorization header for Google's OAuth2 type.

nodes.name: Prepare Document Setup Result
nodes.notes: Normalizes this branch's output to a shape 'Aggregate Document Setup Results' can recognize regardless of whether any documents were actually configured.

nodes.name: Aggregate Document Setup Results
nodes.notes: Discriminates the two converging branches by shape, not by which node ran: real doc-copy results carry a 'doc_result' marker (set in 'Prepare Document Setup Result'), the no-templates skip path doesn't. Produces one summary item either way, with the full matter/config context restored so the task and deadline stages downstream still have what they need.

nodes.name: If Has Task List
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one task configured for this practice area) → create the task checklist in Clio.
No → route to Skip. Both branches converge on 'Aggregate Task Setup Results'.

nodes.name: Skip No Task List
nodes.notes: No standard task list configured for this matter's practice area — no Clio tasks created. Add rows to TASK_LIST_MAP in 'Determine Practice Area Setup Config' if this practice area should have one.

nodes.name: Split Task List Into Items
nodes.notes: Fans out into one item per configured task, with its due date already calculated as calendar days from the matter's open date (not business-day math — task due dates are internal reminders, not court deadlines; see the deadline-calendaring stage for business-day rules).

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ data: { name: $json.task_name, due_at: $json.due_date + 'T00:00:00.000Z', matter: { id: $json.matter_id }, status: 'pending', priority: 'normal' } }) }}

nodes.name: Create Clio Matter Task
nodes.notes:
Creates one Clio task per configured checklist item, linked to the new matter and due-dated from its open date. Same request shape as the Court Deadline Calculator's (NTC-16) 'Update Clio Task API' node.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as the matters fetch above.

'Never Error' is on so one failed task creation doesn't stop the rest of the checklist from being created — check execution history if a task is missing from Clio afterward.

nodes.name: Prepare Task Setup Result
nodes.notes: Normalizes this branch's output to a shape 'Aggregate Task Setup Results' can recognize regardless of whether any tasks were actually configured.

nodes.name: Aggregate Task Setup Results
nodes.notes: Same converge-and-discriminate pattern as 'Aggregate Document Setup Results', one stage over: carries the running config (including doc results already gathered) forward into the deadline stage.

nodes.name: If Has Deadline Rules
nodes.notes:
Yes (at least one intake deadline rule configured for this practice area) → calculate and calendar them.
No → route to Skip. Both branches converge on 'Aggregate Deadline Setup Results'.

nodes.name: Skip No Deadline Rules
nodes.notes: No intake deadline rules configured for this matter's practice area — nothing calendared. Add rows to DEADLINE_RULE_MAP in 'Determine Practice Area Setup Config' if this practice area should have intake deadlines.

nodes.name: Compute Intake Deadlines
nodes.notes: Fans out into one item per configured deadline rule, with the calendar date already calculated from the matter's open date. 'business' offset_type skips weekends and US federal holidays; 'calendar' counts every day. The firm owns and enters every rule in DEADLINE_RULE_MAP — this node only does the date arithmetic, never suggests or interprets a deadline.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ data: { summary: $json.rule_name + ' — ' + $json.matter_display_number, description: $json.description, all_day: true, start_at: $json.deadline_date + 'T00:00:00.000Z', end_at: $json.deadline_date + 'T23:59:59.000Z', matter: { id: $json.matter_id } } }) }}

nodes.name: Create Clio Calendar Deadline
nodes.notes:
Creates one all-day Clio calendar entry per configured deadline rule, linked to the matter. The calendar_entries.json endpoint and field names (summary/description/all_day/start_at/end_at) follow Clio's general REST conventions but weren't confirmed against a live account during authoring — check developer.clio.com and adjust the field names here if your response comes back with an error. If your firm calendars deadlines in Google/Outlook instead of Clio, swap this node for the 'Post to Google Calendar API' / 'Post to Outlook Calendar API' pattern from the Court Deadline Calculator (NTC-16).

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as elsewhere in this workflow.

'Never Error' is on so one failed deadline doesn't block the rest — check execution history if a deadline is missing from Clio afterward.

nodes.name: Prepare Deadline Setup Result
nodes.notes: Normalizes this branch's output to a shape 'Aggregate Deadline Setup Results' can recognize regardless of whether any deadline rules were actually configured.

nodes.name: Aggregate Deadline Setup Results
nodes.notes: Final converge point before the summary — every stage's results (folders, docs, tasks, deadlines) are now present on this single item, whether or not each stage found anything configured to do.

parameters.jsCode:
const r = $input.first().json;

const lines = [
  `New matter opened: ${r.matter_display_number} — ${r.matter_description} (${r.practice_area}).`,
  '',
  `Folder tree: ${r.subfolder_count} folder(s) created under ${r.matter_folder_link}`,
  `  ${r.subfolders_created.join(', ')}`,
  '',
  r.doc_setup_count > 0 ? `${r.doc_setup_count} document template(s) copied in:` : 'No document templates configured for this practice area.',
  ...r.docs_created.map(d => `  • ${d.label} — ${d.link}`),
  '',
  r.task_setup_count > 0 ? `${r.task_setup_count} task(s) assigned in Clio:` : 'No standard task list configured for this practice area.',
  ...r.tasks_created.map(t => `  • ${t.name} — due ${t.due_date}`),
  '',
  r.deadline_setup_count > 0 ? `${r.deadline_setup_count} intake deadline(s) calendared in Clio:` : 'No intake deadline rules configured for this practice area.',
  ...r.deadlines_created.map(d => `  • ${d.name} — ${d.date}`),
];

return [{ json: {
  matter_id: r.matter_id,
  matter_display_number: r.matter_display_number,
  attorney_email: r.attorney_email,
  summary_message: lines.join('\n'),
  summary_subject: `Matter setup complete — ${r.matter_display_number}`,
} }];

nodes.name: Build Matter Setup Summary
nodes.notes: Combines every stage's results (folders, documents, tasks, deadlines) into one summary for the audit log and staff email — the single place a staff member can see everything this workflow did for this matter.

nodes.name: Log Matter Setup To Compliance
nodes.notes:
Logs this matter's full setup to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet — no email sent from this call itself, purely the audit trail. This workflow delivers its summary to staff, not a client, so opt-out checking does not apply here.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable.

nodes.name: Notify Staff Matter Setup Complete
nodes.notes:
Emails staff a plain-text summary of everything set up for the new matter, with a direct link to its Drive folder and every generated document.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)' — reuse if already deployed elsewhere.

main.node: Split Doc Template List Into Items
Copy Doc Template To Matter Folder

description: Watches Clio for newly opened matters and runs the firm's standard opening checklist automatically — creates the matter's folder tree in Google Drive, copies configured internal document templates into it, assigns the firm's standard task list in Clio, and calendars intake deadlines from firm-entered rules. Docs, tasks, and deadlines are all configured per practice area and skipped gracefully if unconfigured. Replaces manual matter-opening checklists and Clio's own templates. Logs every matter setup to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet.
